5165: Chun-Li is a video game character created by Capcom. She is part of the Street Fighter series, and is the first female playable character to appear in a mainstream fighting game.
6723: Ryu is one of the main characters from Capcom's Street Fighter series (and is also one of Capcom's mascot characters) and is the archetypical fighting game protagonist. Ryu has appeared in every Street Fighter game and vs/crossover games produced in part with Capcom.
9223: Gouki is a vicious and aggressive fighter who fights only to test his strength against his opponents. However, being a strict upholder of the code of the warrior, he usually only fights those who challenge him instead of picking fights.
9311: Very little is known about Bison (Vega in the Japanese version). Except that he is the head of Shadowlaw. In contrast to Ken and Ryu's Hadou (which is based in chi), Bison's powers are based in his rage and hatred, and are referred to as his "Psycho Power.
9312: Guile is a Sergeant in the United States Air Force. He has pride in both the Air Force and his men, and frequently goes out drinking with them whenever they can. He and his partner, Nash, have served together for many years in various missions and military conflicts.
9313: Ryu's best friend and the only son of the extremely rich Masters family. He lives in San Francisco with his parents in a very large mansion (it takes 20 minutes to drive from the front yard to the main house). He too spends a lot of time training as well, but not as much as Ryu.
9317: This massive Russian makes up for his obvious mental shortcomings with sheer size and an unadulterated zeal for fighting.
9476: Known as "The Southern Comet", Dee Jay is a cheerful kickboxer who fights to musical rhythm. Eventually, he becomes a music star, though he still has time to enter the second World Warrior tournament to find some new rhythm for his songs.
9477: Honda appears as one of the more prominent characters to appear in the second half of the anime, unlike a majority of the characters that were not heavily involved in the backstory of the game.
9478: He's first seen wrestling with E. Honda in Calcutta to win prize money. Dhalsim manages to slip away from his grip however, and attempts to mentally subdue Honda. Ryu's presence however distracts Dhalsim enough for Honda to regain control of the match and win due to forfeit.
9479: Vega (Balrog in the Japanese version), is one of the bosses of the Street Fighter fighting game series. Vega uses his own fighting style of which is a blend of Ninjutsu and Bullfighting. Vega was born to a noble family in Catalonia, Spain.
9480: Sagat is the World Warrior Champion who loses his title to Ryu and becomes obsessed in defeating him after his loss.
9915: Shadaloo Cammy's early history is unknown; her first appearance in the Street Fighter chronology was Street Fighter Alpha 3, where she was a soulless Doll sent to assassinate Dhalsim.
16914: Fei Long is a fictional character in the Street Fighter series. He made his first appearance in Super Street Fighter II in 1993 as one of the four new characters introduced in the game. In the series, he is a martial artist and action movie star.
36309: This character page is set to represent and list all narrators, which haven't been given a visual representation of themselves in their respective work.
126962: Akira Oono is the silent daughter of the Oono family. Akira is popular at school for being multi-talented but sneaks away to play arcade games to escape the harsh environment at home.
127767: While he starts off as a snarky brat with an ego bigger than any winning streak he could rack up in Street Fighter, he eventually grows out of it. However, he never abandons his dedication and love for gaming, which almost borders on unhealthy obsession.
127808: A girl in Haruo's class throughout junior high. Goes to an all-girl school with Onizuka throughout high school.
132439: He is Yaguchi Haruo's best friend. They became friends in middle school and stayed in the same school all through high school. He is shown to care very much for Haruo.
132441: Reiko is Yaguchi Haruo and Hidaka Koharu's homeroom teacher in Middle School.
132442: Moemi is the personal instructor serving the Ōno Zaibatsu. She at times abuses her powers as an instructor and makes Ono suffer from overworking such as studying and practice with no tolerance of gaming.
132443: Jīya is the butler of the Ouno resident, and the driver serving Ouno Akira. He shows very deep feelings for Akira, being her personal driver for many years.
132444: Genta is one of the Elementary School classmates of Ōno Akira and Yaguchi Haruo. He admires Akira for her beauty, smartness, and the fact that she's rich. He aims to make Akira his fiancé but keeps getting rejected.
188685: He first appeared as a boss character in Street Fighter II. Balrog is self-centered, hot-tempered, arrogant, flippant and sadistic.
222934: A teacher at the Middle School where Yaguchi Haruo, Ōno Akira, and Hidaka Koharu attend.
